0: One Schedule Cannot Serve Every Budget
An exact menu law under signed cancellation, for every m ≥ 5
Rider University  ·  CIG-AMF formal research programme  ·  4 Lean 4 modules, 38 audited declarations, 0 sorry, axioms only {propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound}
20: A schedule reveals items one at a time; a client with budget k sees the first k. How well can a SINGLE schedule — or a small MENU of schedules — serve every budget at once, when the items carry SIGNED weights that cancel?

An ordering is a permutation; the retained prefix at budget k has sum s_k, and the normalised regret is (|s_k| − k mod 2)/D, because every g_i is odd and so min over |S| = k of |Σ g_i| equals k mod 2 by parity.
WHAT IS NOT NEW  (read at theorem level)

Disser, Klimm, Schewior & Weckbecker, arXiv:2305.01310.  Their objective is f : 2^U → ℝ≥0, ACCOUNTABLE, meaning for every X there is e ∈ X with f(X∖{e}) ≥ f(X) − f(X)/|X|.  Thm 1: GreedyScaling attains the best-possible ratio ρ* ≥ 1.  Thm 4: the lower bound 2.246.  Thm 5: a 1.772-competitive randomised algorithm.
The whole incremental-maximisation programme for monotone accountable objectives is PRIOR, as is the idea of one schedule serving every budget. We credit all of it.

THREE SEPARATIONS, AND THE FIRST IS DECISIVE.  (1) CLASS: their codomain is ℝ≥0; our prefix sums go NEGATIVE, so the objective fails the codomain restriction BEFORE accountability is even tested — a class separation, not a constant improvement. (2) METRIC: theirs is multiplicative, ours additive and normalised by D. The numbers are not on the same scale and must never be tabulated together. (3) OBJECT: they ask for ONE ordering; we ask for the MINIMUM MENU.

So dfc IS the normalised numerator, and no index bookkeeping is needed anywhere below. A budget is free iff its prefix sum lies in {−1, 0, 1}; any defect is an even number ≥ 2.
If a schedule pays nothing at any budget, then every single element moves the prefix sum by at most 2. The element 3 is a step that forbids — so EVERY ordering of the family pays at least 2.
This is where the signed structure does the work. A non-negative objective has no analogue of no_big_step, which is the technical reason the prior class cannot host this argument.

13: Under signed cancellation the gap between one schedule and a menu is not a constant factor but an exact function of the population: V_path / V_avg = m − 1, for every m ≥ 5, with both sides attained.

The prior's monotone accountable class cannot host this: its objectives take values in ℝ≥0, and the whole mechanism here rests on prefix sums that go negative. This is a class separation, and no constant of theirs is comparable to any constant of ours.

SCOPE — NOT ESTABLISHED.  (1) ONE family. Not a theorem about arbitrary signed weights. (2) retained_col_sum is an identity EVERY menu satisfies; it singles out no menu, and a prescribed NON-uniform trajectory may exclude the witness and change the value — that case is open. (3) The cyclic menu is chosen for computability, not shown optimal. (4) Step 6 has two hypotheses: balance and concentration. (5) No algorithm, and no competitive ratio in the prior's sense is claimed or computed.
